description: Comprehensive list of features and requirements for a complete systems and algorithmic programming language, distilled from multi-language comparisons (Java, NASM/FASM, Fortran, C, Rust). Use this prompt to guide deep analysis and design decisions.

requirements: Variables and assignment for storing and changing state
Conditional branching: if/else, compare and jump
Looping and recursion: while, for, goto, function recursion
Basic I/O: reading input and writing output

primitive_types: Signed integers: i8, i16, i32, i64, i128
Unsigned integers: u8, u16, u32, u64, u128
composite_types: Array and slice types with length and element type
Struct or record types with named fields
Function types treating functions as values
pointer_reference_types: Raw pointer type *T for direct memory access
Pointer-sized integer type usize for pointer arithmetic
advanced_features: Static type checking rather than dynamic typing
Trait or interface system for ad‑hoc polymorphism
Coercion rules: when implicit conversions occur
Defined integer overflow behaviour: panic, wrap, saturate

memory_regions: Stack for local variables and call frames
Heap for dynamic allocation with lifetime beyond function scope
Data section for initialised global/static data

heap_management_strategies.manual: malloc/free style (C, assembly) providing speed but risk of leaks and use‑after‑free
heap_management_strategies.garbage_collection: automatic memory reclamation with pause times (Java, Go)
heap_management_strategies.reference_counting: automatic management with cycle issues (Swift, Python)
heap_management_strategies.arena_region: bulk freeing and cache‑friendly patterns (Zig, custom allocators)

alignment_layout: Struct padding and explicit layout control
Cache line alignment (e.g. 64‑byte lines on x86‑64)
Ability to query sizeof and offsetof for types
volatile_and_ordering: Volatile qualifiers to prevent compiler reordering around I/O mapped memory
Memory ordering semantics: acquire, release, sequential consistency
Memory fences/barriers at assembly level (MFENCE, LFENCE, SFENCE)

advanced_constructs: Infinite loops with break returning a value
Goto or labelled breaks for low‑level code generation
Iterator style loops (for i in range)
Do‑while loops guaranteeing at least one execution
non_local_flow: Result or Option types for functional error handling
Long jump mechanisms (setjmp/longjmp) as unsafe constructs
Coroutines and generators for cooperative scheduling
error_handling_strategies: Exceptions with stack unwinding and catch blocks
Result/Option types to force explicit handling

function_system.definition: Functions must have a name, parameter list, return type and body; first‑class functions treat functions as values

SystemV_AMD64.args: rdi, rsi, rdx, rcx, r8, r9 then stack
SystemV_AMD64.caller_saved: rax, rcx, rdx, rsi, rdi, r8–r11

Windows_x64.args: rcx, rdx, r8, r9 then stack

advanced_features: Closures and lambdas capturing outer variables
Inline functions to suggest no call frame

features: Modules and namespaces with explicit import/export
Name collision avoidance via namespace scoping
Cycle detection and error reporting in module dependencies
Package system with version constraints and registries

standard_io: print/eprint functions for stdout and stderr
file_io: Open files with path and mode
io_system.syscall_interface: Direct invocation of OS syscalls (e.g. Linux syscall with mov rax, rdi, rsi, etc.) or via wrapper functions

math: power and roots: pow, sqrt, cbrt
trigonometric functions: sin, cos, tan and inverses
Greatest common divisor and least common multiple
string: Parsing from and converting to numeric types
collections: Arrays and slices for contiguous memory
Hash maps and hash sets for O(1) access
Stacks and queues built on top of dynamic arrays

pipeline: Linking to produce executable or library
build_systems: Cargo-like integrated build and dependency tools

abi_interoperability.c_abi: Ability to declare and call functions with C linkage for interop with libc and OS APIs
abi_interoperability.ffi: Foreign function interface to call into external libraries and expose functions to other languages

meta_programming.macro_system: Support for macros: textual substitution (C style) and hygienic macros (Rust style)
meta_programming.generics_templates: Parametric types and functions with monomorphisation or dynamic dispatch
meta_programming.compile_time_evaluation: Constant expressions and compile‑time function evaluation

algorithm_features.simd_intrinsics: Intrinsic functions for SSE/AVX and portable SIMD abstractions
algorithm_features.iterators: Lazy iterators with functional combinators (map, filter, fold)
algorithm_features.pattern_matching: Match expression with guards and range patterns

formal_specification.grammar: EBNF grammar defining program, declarations, statements, expressions, types and blocks
formal_specification.type_rules: Inference rules specifying typing of expressions and statements
formal_specification.operational_semantics: Formal evaluation order and side effect semantics
formal_specification.undefined_behavior: Inventory of operations that are undefined, implementation‑defined or unspecified

development_roadmap.current_status: Lexer, parser, AST, symbol table, semantic checks and simple stack‑based NASM emitter implemented
missing_features: Full type system including floats, structs, arrays and pointers
Function calls with proper calling convention and recursion
Proper ELF symbol export and linking
